CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Respond to the escalating U.S. trade offensive with a calibrated, proportionate retaliation — targeted duties on politically sensitive U.S. exports (notably agriculture) plus a formal WTO challenge — while keeping the door open to negotiations and avoiding a full escalation spiral. We should not pre-emptively capitulate on forced technology-transfer or Made in China 2025, but we should also avoid broad retaliatory tariffs that would damage our own export economy and hand Washington the confrontation it appears to want.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is high but not yet existential. The U.S. has already signed Section 232 steel (25%) and aluminum (10%) tariffs (timeline 2018-03-08), Trump has declared 'trade wars are good, and easy to win' (2018-03-02), and by 2018-03-21 press reporting confirms the White House is hours away from announcing Section 301 tariffs on ~$60 billion of Chinese goods explicitly to 'punish' China's technology-transfer practices and to 'inflict maximum harm,' with Lighthizer openly stating Chinese retaliation 'would be inevitable' (CNBC, 2018-03-21; POLITICO, 2018-03-07). This directly threatens key export sectors (aerospace, ICT, machinery) and China's tech self-sufficiency goals — the +0.5 anchor. The threat is tempered because tariffs on Chinese goods have not yet actually been imposed at decision date and the ~$60B figure is bounded by the §301 harm finding, so the full export-economy shock is prospective rather than material. On action: the steel/aluminum duties already signed give China legitimate grounds for immediate, proportionate retaliation now, and the Cov analysis documents Beijing's own signaling in this direction (self-initiated sorghum anti-dumping probe) plus readiness to pursue WTO dispute settlement. A measured retaliation affirms resolve and defends the multilateral order without feeding the 'trade war is easy to win' narrative, so action_score sits at a mild escalatory level (-0.3) rather than maximal escalation.
key_factors: Section 301 findings/tariffs on ~$60B of Chinese goods imminent (CNBC 3/21 report)
Direct US targeting of China's technology-transfer regime and Made in China 2025
US signaling of coordinated pressure (US/EU/Japan talks on China IP)
Tariffs on Chinese goods not yet applied; shock still prospective
China signaling measured response: WTO challenge + targeted probes (Cov analysis)
